---
title: "Example report"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
```

This is the report `render_report()` produces, run against the synthetic
hospital database bundled with the package: 46 tables and 523 columns from a
fictional NHS trust, capped at 1,000 rows per table. It is regenerated every
time the site is built, so it always reflects the current package.

The report shows headline counts, the table inventory ranked by size and
freshness, the type and semantic-type mix, null and uniqueness distributions,
candidate duplicate columns, the full searchable column profile and the run
log. Identifier, free-text and personal-data columns have their literal values
suppressed, which is the default.

<p><a href="../example-report.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the report in its own window</a></p>

<iframe src="../example-report.html" title="Example DBinventory report"
        style="width: 100%; height: 85vh; border: 1px solid #dee2e6; border-radius: 4px;"
        loading="lazy"></iframe>

To make one for your own database:

```r
library(DBinventory)
inventory_run("Driver={ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server};Server=...;Database=...;Trusted_Connection=yes;",
              store = "dw_inventory.sqlite", report = "dw_inventory.html")
```
